title: A Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of Co-Reconstituted TrenibotulinumtoxinE and OnabotulinumtoxinA in Adult Participants With Moderate to Severe Upper Facial Lines
official: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Co-Reconstituted TrenibotulinumtoxinE and OnabotulinumtoxinA for the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Upper Facial Lines in Adults
summary: The objective of this Phase 2 study is to assess the safety and efficacy of single treatment of trenibotulinumtoxinE and onabotulibumtoxinA combination in adult participants with moderate to severe upper facial lines. The study has two parts; Part 1 evaluates treatment for glabellar lines.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* For glabellar lines (GL) indication: participant must have moderate or severe GL at maximum furrow as assessed by both the investigator and participant using the AGLSS at Screening and Baseline (Day 1) visits.
* Participant must be in good health as per investigator's judgment based on medical history, physical examination, vital sign measurements, 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) parameters, clinical laboratory evaluations, and neurological assessment.
* In the investigator's opinion, participant must not have a condition or be in a situation that may put the participant at significant risk, may confound the study results, or may interfere significantly with the participant's participation in the study.

Exclusion Criteria:

* For GL Indication: Severe GL at rest as assessed by the investigator using the AGLSS at Screening or Baseline (Day 1).
* History of immunization to any botulinum neurotoxin serotype or hypersensitivity to any botulinum neurotoxin serotype or any other constituents of the study drug or its excipients
* Active infection or dermatological condition at the treatment injection sites.
* Medical condition that may put the subject at increased medical risk with exposure to botulinum toxin, including diagnosed myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton syndrome, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or any other condition that might interfere with neuromuscular function
